item.title: Self-calibration of the neutrino-argon cross section with solar neutrinos
item.description: The success of DUNE’s MeV physics program depends upon high-precision knowledge of the charged-current (CC) νe+Ar40 cross section. While there are indirect constraints on the cross section with uncertainties at the ∼10% level, the only direct measurement in the MeV range disagrees by more than a factor of two. We show, surprisingly, that this cross section can be precisely measured using the solar-neutrino data themselves. This is possible because of independent knowledge of the B8 flux and survival probability, plus the distinctive angular distributions of the Fermi and Gamow-Teller transitions that comprise the cross section. We propose new methods to extract the transition strengths, considering both intuitive groupings and a principal component analysis. Assuming pessimistic detection performance but controlled detector systematic uncertainties, we demonstrate that a precision of ≲2% on the cross section can be achieved in the 9–15 MeV energy range. item.title: Singlet-doublet dark matter beyond freeze-out
item.description: The singlet-doublet fermion model of dark matter is an economical weak-scale dark matter model that realizes the dark matter abundance through interactions with the electroweak bosons of the Standard Model. Depending on the size of the Yukawa couplings in the model, the dark matter relic abundance can be produced via freeze-out (including coannihilation), coscattering, freeze-in, or the SuperWIMP mechanism. We analyze the ways this model can realize the dark matter density with emphasis on the small Yukawa coupling regime. In this limit, direct and indirect detection are difficult, but a rich collider phenomenology is possible.

item.title: Quark-level CPT violation in neutral-meson systems
item.description: This work investigates CPT and Lorentz breakdown in neutral-meson interferometry within the nonminimal Standard-Model Extension. Employing methods of chiral perturbation theory for mass dimension d=5, a connection between the quark-level and the meson effective pseudoscalar Lagrangian is established. The resulting phenomenological signatures in neutral-meson oscillations with particular focus on the detector geometry are explored. This analysis permits the interpretation of such CPT tests within the d=5 quark sector of the Standard-Model Extension. Existing data are used to extract first constraints on two coefficients and to estimate achievable sensitivity gains over published bounds of up to 18 orders of magnitude.

item.title: Probing the electron Yukawa coupling with resonant Higgs boson production at FCC-ee in e^+e^-→ H → WW^* lepton-plus-jets final states
item.description: We report a detailed simulation study of the search for s-channel Higgs boson production in e^+e^-collisions at a center-of-mass (c.m.) energy of sqrts=125,textrmGeV at the CERN Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee), as a means to constrain the electron Yukawa coupling, y_e . The process of interest is e^+e^-→ H→ WW^*→ ell ^± ν + jj with four different WW^* final states considered, involving both on-and off-shell W bosons decaying either into dileptons ( ell ^± = e^± and μ ^± , including those from τ ^± decays) or into dijets (jj). Signal and background events are discriminated through a multiclass gradient boosted decision tree exploiting a comprehensive set of kinematic and topological variables across the four final-state categories. item.title: Inclusive mathrm psi (2S) production at midrapidity in pp collisions at sqrts = 13 TeV
item.description: Inclusive production of mathrm psi (2S) mesons is measured at midrapidity ( |y| < 0.9 ) in pp collisions at sqrts = 13 TeV using the ALICE detector at the LHC, extending the available midrapidity coverage towards lower transverse-momentum ( p_textrmT ). The measurement is performed in the p_textrmT range of 4 to 16 GeV/ c and is based on events triggered by the Transition Radiation Detector, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 1.7 ± 1.8% (syst.) pb ^-1 . The p_textrmT-differential production cross section of the mathrm psi (2S) and its ratio to the mathrm J/psi production cross section are presented. The results extend the accessible p_textrmT range down to 4 GeV/ c , and a mild rise of the mathrm psi (2S)-to-mathrm J/psi cross section ratio with increasing p_textrmT is observed. The measurements are compared with theoretical predictions based on NRQCD and the ICEM model.
item.author: et al.

item.title: Search for dark matter produced in association with a dark Higgs boson decaying into a bottom quark–antiquark pair in proton–proton collisions at sqrts=13,text Tehspace-.08emtext V
item.description: A search for dark matter produced in association with a dark Higgs boson decaying into a bottom quark–antiquark pair has been performed using proton–proton collision data at a center-of-mass energy of 13 ,text Tehspace-.08emtext V . The search uses data collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC during the 2016–2018 data-taking period, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 ,text fb^-1 . The results are interpreted in terms of a theoretical model of dark matter production that, together with a spin-1 text Z^prime boson mediator, predicts the existence of a Higgs-boson-like particle in the dark sector (i.e., a dark Higgs boson). This search focuses on an experimental signature with large missing transverse momentum from dark matter production and a resonant structure in the invariant mass of the bottom quark–antiquark pair from the dark Higgs boson decay. item.title: Gravitational effective theories with maximal supersymmetry and a peculiar parity
item.description: We study the space of four-dimensional ultraviolet completions for mathcalN = 8 supergravity that are described at low energies by weakly-coupled effective field theories (EFTs) with maximal supersymmetry and SU(4) × SU(4) R-symmetry. We show that tree-level factorization of the 4-, 5-, and 6-point EFT scattering amplitudes, together with a certain “peculiar parity” condition, leads to nonlinear constraints on the 4-point Wilson coefficients. This peculiar parity is a property that can only be imposed on a subset of scalar amplitudes. Combining the nonlinear constraints with positivity, we find that the allowed region of 4-point Wilson coefficients is reduced to a non-convex domain with two sharp corners: one being the closed superstring Virasoro-Shapiro amplitude, the other an infinite spin tower amplitude exchanging states of every spin at the same mass. item.title: Nonabelian Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture and monopole confinement
item.description: Within the known landscape of quantum gravity, most theories satisfy the Lattice Weak Gravity Conjecture (LWGC), which requires a superextremal particle at every site in the electric charge lattice Γ. However, counterexamples to the LWGC exist, and it was recently hypothesized that such counterexamples necessarily feature fractionally charged confined monopoles. In this work, we verify this hypothesis in toroidal orbifold compactifications of the heterotic string, which notably feature LWGC violation in both the abelian and nonabelian gauge sectors. In all the cases we consider, there exists a discrete subgroup of the center of the gauge group K ⊆ Z(G) such that superextremal particles exist at every site in the charge lattice of the quotient group G/K, while (confined) monopoles exist at all sites in the magnetic charge lattice of G/K. item.title: Every 3D Conformal Field Theory Has an LΛw1+∞ Symmetry
item.description: A one-parameter family of deformed Lw1+∞ soft symmetry algebras acting on tree-level gravitational theories in AdS4 has recently been discovered; it is denoted LΛw1+∞. Here, we show that all CFT3 s, including those dual to quantum gravity on AdS4, admit an LΛw1+∞ action generated by the ANEC operator, its conformal descendants, and their commutators. This extends previous tree-level results on these soft symmetries to the strongly coupled quantum regime.

item.title: Improved approximations for collective neutrino oscillations
item.description: A one-and two-body su(n) Hamiltonian governing the dynamics of many systems, including collective neutrino oscillations, is investigated. We start by analyzing the algebraic structure(u(nN)), formulate a product structure of the algebra, and utilize this to construct generic expressions for operator expectation values, Rényi Entropy, and Wigner Functions. Performing the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy truncation we develop a systematic methodology for going beyond the mean field with polynomial scaling on a classical computer.

item.title: Evidence for ηc(2S)→pp¯π+π−π0 and observation of χcJ→pp¯π+π−π0
item.description: Using (2.712±0.014)×109 ψ(3686) events collected by the BESIII detector at the BEPCII collider, the ψ(3686)→γpp¯π+π−π0 process is investigated. Evidence for the decay of ηc(2S)→pp¯π+π−π0 is found with a signal significance of 3.3σ. The product of branching fractions of B[ψ(3686)→γηc(2S)]×B[ηc(2S)→pp¯π+π−π0] is determined to be (3.4±0.5±0.8)×10−6, where the first uncertainty is statistical and the second systematic. The hadronic decays of χcJ→pp¯π+π−π0(J=0,1,2) are observed, and their branching fractions are measured to be B(χc0→pp¯π+π−π0)=(4.79±0.01±0.40)×10−3, B(χc1→pp¯π+π−π0)=(2.13 ± 0.01 ± 0.17)×10−3, and B(χc2→pp¯π+π−π0)=(3.72 ± 0.01±0.29)×10−3, respectively. Furthermore, the branching fractions for the intermediate processes χcJ→pp¯ω are updated with significantly improved precision: B(χc0→pp¯ω)=(5.76 ± 0.01 ± 0.42)×10−4, B(χc1→pp¯ω)=(1.85 ± 0.01 ± 0.13)×10−4, and B(χc2→pp¯ω)=(4.51±0.01±0.33)×10−4, respectively.

item.title: Quantum channel capacity of traversable wormholes
item.description: We formulate the Gao-Jafferis-Wall traversable wormhole protocol as a quantum channel and compute its quantum channel capacity. We show that this capacity is governed by the time derivative of an out-of-time-ordered correlator, hence by operator size growth in the holographic dual, and that its growth is bounded above by the Einstein gravity limit. The channel capacity therefore provides a natural benchmark for quantum simulations of traversable wormholes.

item.title: Observation of an altered a0(980) line shape in D+→π+ηη
item.description: Using 20.3 fb−1 of e+e− collision data collected with the BESIII detector at s=3.773 GeV, we perform the first amplitude analysis of the decay D+→π+ηη. The intermediate process D+→a0(980)+η, a0(980)+→π+η, is the only component retained in the nominal amplitude model, and its branching fraction is measured to be (3.67±0.12stat±0.06syst)×10−3. The π+η mass spectrum associated with a0(980)+η production exhibits a line shape that differs substantially from those observed in D(s)→a0(980)π and D0→a0(980)−e+νe decays. We examine several conventional descriptions of the a0(980) amplitude, including Flatté, dispersively modified Flatté, T-matrix, and K-matrix parametrizations. With reference a0(980) parameters, neither these models nor their extensions including additional small resonant or nonresonant amplitudes reproduce the observed line shape satisfactorily. item.title: Exploring scalar leptoquarks at muon collider via indirect signatures and right-handed neutrino-assisted decays
item.description: Scalar leptoquarks (sLQs) appear in a wide range of ultraviolet-motivated extensions of the Standard Model and provide a natural link between the quark and lepton sectors. In this work, we investigate the discovery potential of an sLQ doublet R˜2(3,2,1/6) that couples to light quarks and right-handed neutrinos (RHNs) at the proposed muon collider. We analyze both indirect probes—arising from t-channel sLQ exchange that affects the high-pT behavior of dijet spectra—and direct searches exploiting pair and single production of the sLQs, incorporating the full interplay of kinematic thresholds and decay topologies. We find that indirect probes at muon colliders deliver remarkably robust sensitivity to the sLQ-quark-muon coupling over a broad mass range. Assuming a sub-O(1) Yukawa coupling, we achieve a 5σ sensitivity up to sLQ masses ∼4.0 TeV (7.0 TeV) at s=5(10) TeV center-of-mass energy with L=3 ab−1 (10 ab−1) integrated luminosity. item.title: Kernel transformations and bounds for smeared spectral functions
item.description: This work develops a framework for transforming between smeared spectral functions computed using different smearing kernels. The kernel-transformation problem naturally arises when information is available for one family of energy-smeared observables, while phenomenology or comparison with other calculations require a different smearing. For exact transformations, analytic conditions are established for the maps to exist and converge without arbitrary regularization. Explicit expressions are provided for several kernel classes of interest, including Cauchy-to-Gaussian transformations and Gaussian-to-Cauchy width mixtures. When exact transformations are unavailable, the inverse problem is tackled through regulated maps paired with bounds on the associated systematic error, directly computable from the given input data. item.title: Nonthermal leptogenesis via cosmological gravitational particle production is tested by inflationary gravitational waves
item.description: We explore the coincidence of scales between cosmic inflation and right-handed neutrinos in seesaw models. We show that inflation models, which will be tested by next-generation cosmic microwave background experiments, can produce right-handed neutrinos in sufficient abundance to explain the observed baryon asymmetry of the Universe. The model can be tested by gravitational wave signatures from cosmic inflation and particle production.

item.title: Crossover or first-order? Regularization effects in a contact interaction treatment * Supported by the Natural Science Foundation of Jiangsu Province (BK20220122); the National Natural Science Foundation of China (12233002), and the Program of China Scholarship Council (202606190076)
item.description: The equation of state of hot and dense, strongly interacting quark matter plays a fundamental role in many areas. However, owing to the nonperturbative nature of strong interactions, a reliable treatment remains under debate. We use a symmetry-preserving treatment of a vector otimes vector contact interaction to study related issues at nonzero temperature or quark chemical potential, and we carefully compare a three-momentum cutoff with a proper-time regularization scheme. The numerical results show that the character of the phase transition in the present model depends sensitively on the regularization scheme and parameter choices.
